**Conclusion: A.** Under the suspect's account he never resisted the arrest itself. He struck the officer only to stop nightstick blows, and if the arrest was unlawful, the common-law privilege to resist it also supports acquittal. D fails under the suspect's account because self-defense against excessive force defeats the assault charge regardless of lawfulness. B reaches the same acquittal on the suspect's account, so the choice between A and B is close, and I switched to A because the team's note points to it.

CONFIDENCE: 50
